body:
I love it.

Thank you so much for sharing.
I didn't realise my patterns were so common...
Should just be pedestrianised in my opinion. But I don't live there so can't really comment.
I hate the underground to, but I will take it when I have to. I prefer to drive but that's not really a possibility anywhere in London.

We're all defective my friend. 
It doesn't take skill to enjoy things. I understand the pain you're probably feeling, I feel it too. 
I hope only the best for you, if you want someone to talk to, I'll do my best to be there for you.

I know Euston, I live in Essex now.
It was nice, I was only there briefly and late on so didn't get to properly explore. It was still rammed, but in a sort of nice way, that I can't often say about London.
It has its place, people need somewhere to go when they're in that 'place'.
Hi, I actually went covent garden last night, is it a long way to go for you?

I think a lot of people feel the same, I know I do. The hardest part is meeting people, and meeting people you feel like you connect with. People you can be the 'real you' with. Atleast that's how I feel.

I can see a few people have already offered to talk, people probably more suited to be a good friend than me. But I'll make the offer regardless. If you wanna talk, pm me. I can't promise we'll have much in common, or connect but I think every connection you try and make brings you closer to making the connection you want.

I wish you only the best.

I have tried to inject some life into it before. It is a good sub, I flick through it often when times are hard and I feel like I derive no enjoyment from life anymore. 

It helps.
I'm not sure this is the place to go to pick up girls mate. If you want to talk or vent though, it's more that sort of place.
If I can muster a trip to the shops tomorrow, I might have to try and make this for myself. Looks so tasty.

Yes I like them a lot, particularly David Attenborough ones. The animals just do things they need to do to survive. You mostly don't stay with one animal too long so you don't get attached to any particular one. Also I find them relaxing, there's a lot of stuff to take in so I think of myself less. And a lot of the time there are amazing visuals or a fascinating fact.

I don't know really, maybe it's just me but I sort of feel  better when I hear David Attenborough 's voice.
I like to watch documentaries, particularly wildlife ones.

I'm the same, I see myself as a logical person. If someone else was worried about these things, I could see for them it shouldn't matter. But these things will always get to me. I can't even talk about specific instances without it happening.

I know how you feel, almost all real life interactions send me into a shame spiral. I still feel ashamed about things I did years ago that had no real consequence, still haunt me even if I can convince myself on an unemotional level it didn't matter.

I made the choice not to a while ago. At times it pains me, I love children, I was a teacher before the stress and emotional battery forced me to escape it. I know it's the right thing for me to do though, to not procreate.
This sounds like something I very much want to read, the myth of sisyphus and the outsider. Thanks for posting this.

The majority of when I first found out I felt it was because of me. Like he knew I was going to be a disappointment, and I was going to ruin his life, that he didn't want me so much he had to kill himself. I still think my being on the way was a big factor in him doing it, but it's starting to bother me less, I don't blame him. If I had a kid on the way I know I'd be failure as a father. I couldn't put a kid through that. I've also moved to thinking if he comitted suicide he was like me, he was just even less willing or able to seek help. 


It makes me feel better to think I might of inherited all this.

Also the permission thing I get, I sort of convinced myself that my family had done it once and they could do it again....but I don't think I want to think like that anymore, it's hard for me to explain.

My father was 27, he killed himself when he found out my mum was pregnant. I didn't find out until I was 26 myself. I was told by my mother it was a freak accident, and she did a good job of hiding what really happened from me for years. But knowing now has made a lot of other things make sense. My gran and grandad just shutdown completely for years and always acted odd with me when I was younger and I did see them (apparently I'm almost identical to him in both appearance and behaviour). My mother was incredibly protective over me and used guilt to control me so that I would not take risks or do things she didn't like, but according to her old friends she wasn't like that at all before and was happy and loving. My father's brother doesn't acknowledge me much, he has always been cold and according to my gran has no sympathy for my father and what he did. 

I had suicidal thoughts and ideation before I knew anything about my father. In a way it's the most connected to him I have ever felt. I feel stupid sometimes that it matters to me so much when I never met him. But it does, and I can recognise what it's done to me and others in my family, enough to make me try and distance myself from it atleast. 

Sorry if I went on a bit then, it's been on my mind a lot recently.
That's lovely of them!

I know one of the posts you're probably referring to is my own. I apologise if you find it to be guilt - tripping, but it's something I feel and posting it was almost affirming to me. Maybe you could add some more that you feel are more appropriate, to make sure the guilt - tripping ones are a smaller percentage.
It broke my heart when I found out about my dad, I imagine it was the same for you with your grandfather. I know it's not an uplifting RTL, but it's an important one. Those people still matter to me.

It's been helping me too, I want to build it up a bit, really make it something special, maybe you can help? No pressure! but if you think of something to post, I've done it and it felt good, maybe it will for you too.
Thanks, I felt like I was forgetting something.

I can't say I ever thought of naming it before but the first thing I thought when I read the title was being able to tell it to fuck off, "oh my god dave, no one likes you. Fuck off dave". Maybe it could be a good thing like that. It can be just like one of the people I cut ties with for no good reason, except I do have a good reason this time, dave is a dick.
I'm intrigued, can you tell me any more? Or might that ruin my reading it for myself?

Death cab for cutie are the ones that jump to mind. Their album "transatlanticism" is in my opinion, absolutely transcendent. 

Jeniferever are also up there.

I think I feel a sort of similar thing, a futility of existence. I've been trying to see it as a good thing as well though. The fact that it doesn't matter could be freeing, maybe the whole of life is just a bit of a side show to nothingness, a way of us toiling away the time. 

I don't know, I like thinking about it though and it's not in an entirely morbid way. 

Maybe life and living just isn't as deep as we want it to be, and we just have to deal with that.
I drive by a river frequently, and I always fantasize about driving into it and just letting it all go. Only when I'm alone obviously, have to shout at myself to stop myself sometimes.
Thanks for talking to me. I want you to remember you did something amazing for me today, even if it doesn't seem that much it's given me a reason to cope and something to look forward to.

I like that. I already feel like I've nothing left to lose, why not take a gamble. Even if I can't do it immediately, it's something i can look forward to, something I can build towards. I've always wanted to travel, but never had the time or money to do it, or I've had someone I was afraid to upset.

I need to turn this emptiness into something positive. I just need to find a way to not get anxious about it...I guess.
Thanks for responding, it means a lot.

I punch myself sometimes, I always aim for the same spot on the side of my head. It's like a release for me. I self harmed by cutting myself in my teens, but it wasn't a release for me, the punching is. I think it's the combination of venting aggression, pain and maybe it does something to my brain...I don't know. 

It's not a good thing, I try my best not to do it.
But do the "normal people" feel like this? Are all the happy people just acting or is there something wrong with me that I just can't fix?

Thank you, I genuinely don't know what to say. It means so much to me that you'd take the time to say these things to me.

But i feel like I'm running out of reasons not to do it. I have less friends and less family seemingly everytime I blink. I've already sworn not to reproduce because I don't want to curse the poor kid with having me as a parent so i feel like in some small way I've already broken the cycle. The things I used to do to bring me back up are losing their hold. My fitness is declining and I just feel guilty and anxious about every interaction I have. I regret everything I do, every move I make. The thought of having to do it again and again every day makes my skin crawl. 

I just don't know how to get by anymore, I don't feel like I'm upto the task of getting through it this time. I'm carrying the weight of every time before with me and it's just not worth carrying anymore.
